parts.text: In contrast to most computer model simulations, we did not find the land carbon sink increasing over time to keep pace with increasing

fuel emissions. We did, however, find a larger ocean carbon sink than predicted by most models, and we found that it has been increasing as emissions grow.

Where is the climate headed?

If these trends in carbon

continue, then in the coming decades, humans will be relying more heavily on the oceans to slow down climate change. But in the next few decades, there are reasons to believe the oceans could become less effective at absorbing carbon.

For example,

waters are not able to hold as much gas, such as carbon dioxide. Warmer surface waters are also less efficient at mixing into the deep ocean, which has the beneficial effect of locking carbon dioxide away from the atmosphere for many

of years.

The data for the past decade hints at the possibility that while the ocean carbon sink is increasing now, its rate of increase may be slowing down.

Carbon cycle models need to improve

For the oceans, most computer models agree with each other, but, for the

period, they do not match our oxygen-based results. For the land, models vary widely from each other, and most do not match our oxygen-based results.

Computer models are essential to provide governments with
scenarios to avoid dangerous climate change, but to be effective they need to be better grounded in what real-world observations are showing. Nature is difficult to represent with a series of

, and observations are few considering the size of the planet.

Looking ahead

We believe our study improves understanding of global carbon sinks and can help lead to more reliable projections of what might happen with climate change in the coming decades. But like any

approach, our oxygen method also has drawbacks.

The measurements themselves are challenging, such that only about 10 research laboratories in the world are routinely doing them. Calibrating the measurements is an

challenge. Earth is not helping: Warmer waters hold less gas, meaning that as oceans warm in response to climate change, they expel some oxygen into the atmosphere. We must account for this in our carbon sink calculations. And to take into account
in ocean circulation and other ocean processes, we have to average our results over 10-year time frames.

reading.title: 主旨、理解与信息定位
reading.instruction: 阅读原文后回答 5 道选择题：1 道主旨、1 道内容理解、1 道段落细节、2 道信息定位。段落细节题以题干指定段落为准。

questions.prompt: Which statement best summarises the overall focus of this article?
options: Oceans and forests have slowed warming by absorbing carbon, but their future capacity is uncertain.
New tracking technologies are changing knowledge of bird migration and opportunities for conservation.
Research documents an increase in foggy days in southern Australia and explores its causes.
Past El Niño erosion shows why California's vulnerable coastline remains at risk.
questions.explanation: 把标题与全文各段的中心内容连起来判断主旨，避免把同一主题下的其他话题当成本文重点。
questions.evidence: If the oceans and forests keep absorbing the same amount of carbon dioxide, scientists will have a sense of what to expect in the future and what can be done to slow climate change.

questions.prompt: Why is understanding continued carbon absorption by forests and oceans useful?
options: It removes every uncertainty about future weather.
It proves that burning fossil fuels has no consequences.
It helps scientists anticipate future conditions and responses to climate change.
It means climate change has permanently stopped.
questions.explanation: 第 5 段提供了作答依据。正确选项用不同说法表达了文中的信息；请比较范围、数量、因果关系与限定词。
questions.evidence: If the oceans and forests keep absorbing the same amount of carbon dioxide, scientists will have a sense of what to expect in the future and what can be done to slow climate change.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is explicitly made in paragraph 12?
options: This is because many parts of the land and ocean don’t behave in the same ways.
Computer models can help overcome some of these complexities, but they too have limitations.
Earth is not helping: Warmer waters hold less gas, meaning that as oceans warm in response to climate change, they expel some oxygen into the atmosphere.
For the oceans, most computer models agree with each other, but, for the historical period, they do not match our oxygen-based results.
questions.explanation: 定位第 12 段，比较四个选项的具体信息。其余选项来自本文其他段落，并非本段明确陈述的内容。
questions.evidence: Computer models can help overcome some of these complexities, but they too have limitations.
